title: Fridge, yogurt drink beside the milk
goal: Get a yogurt drink from the fridge
expect: Step 1 takes the yogurt drink (white bottle, pink cap, labeled YOGURT DRINK), not the milk
Says how to tell the yogurt drink from the milk (the pink cap, the label, or the taller milk bottle with the blue cap)
Has a mistake for taking the milk instead of the yogurt drink
Does not ask the learner to open the fridge: it is already open
Every done-when is a state a camera can see (how the yogurt drink looks and where it is), not an action
style: A photorealistic photo taken by the camera of a head-mounted display worn by a person standing in a home kitchen: first person, at eye height, looking slightly down, natural indoor light, a slightly wide lens, a little sensor noise. No people, no hands, no text overlays, no watermark. Printed labels are plain block capitals and spelled exactly as given.
views: An open refrigerator seen from one step in front of it, its door swung open to the left. On the middle shelf, near the center of the frame: a white plastic bottle with a bright pink cap and a printed label that reads YOGURT DRINK stands touching, on its right, a slightly taller white plastic bottle with a blue cap and a label that reads MILK. The two bottles have the same shape and color apart from the caps, labels and height, so they are easy to confuse. Around them: a carton of eggs on the top shelf, a glass jar of jam and a block of butter on the middle shelf, a few apples in the crisper drawer at the bottom, and a ketchup bottle in the door.

The same refrigerator with the same objects in the same places, photographed a moment later by the same head-mounted camera after the person moved their head a little to the left and leaned slightly closer: the view shifts, and the YOGURT DRINK and MILK bottles are a bit larger and slightly right of center. Keep every object, label, color and position as in the attached photo.
